## TL;DR

I exercised the four requested Agents tabs in headless WebKit from a detached
scratch checkout served by `just serve-noauth`. All four routes rendered at
1280px and 375px, with no horizontal document overflow at mobile width. During
error-path checks I found that schedule failures and detected-agent update
failures were not announced to assistive technology. I added alert/status live
regions and regression tests. The preview server rejected direct writes with
HTTP 405 because preview children are read-only. A Playwright in-memory API
stub verified browser save/reload flows at both viewport widths; that does not
prove backend durability.

## Work and rationale

The task is a QA pass, so I began by reading the task file and tracing the four
tab panels and their data flows. Existing fixtures made it possible to inspect
populated scheduled-task and reminder states without changing stored data. I
used the fixture query for the seeded schedule list and the due-reminder list,
then also loaded the server-backed schedule list to confirm the panel works
with actual repository data. Team cards and detected-agent rows populated from
the scratch checkout's config and PATH snapshot.

I created a detached scratch worktree beneath the assigned task worktree and
ran `just serve-noauth 7278` there. This kept the active task checkout out of
the server process, as required, and avoided modifying the main checkout. All
browser sessions were headless Playwright WebKit. At 1280×900 and 375×812, I
visited each tab route. Every tab rendered its expected content; at 375px the
document scroll width matched the viewport width. The reminder editor also
measured 375px wide when open on the mobile viewport.

The interaction pass exposed an environment constraint as well as an
accessibility issue. Creating a schedule produced HTTP 405 with the response
`preview servers are read-only`; the entered form remained open and the error
was visible. Creating a reminder produced the same 405 response and visible
error, and the editor remained at the viewport width. RepoOS preview child
servers deliberately reject every non-GET request, so real filesystem
persistence could not be observed in this mandated setup. I kept actual server
data untouched. I then used Playwright route handlers to provide an in-memory
API store across reloads while the app remained served from the required
auth-less instance. Ross instruction edits, schedule create/edit, and reminder
create/edit reappeared after reload at 1280px and 375px. This verifies the
browser-side flow with successful API responses, not backend durability.

The schedule list and editor rendered their errors as plain text with the
`.ff-error` styling, but did not identify them as alerts. I added `role="alert"`
to both schedule failure surfaces. I also found that a failed detected-agent
update check displayed a message without a live region. I added `role="status"`
to that message; this describes a recoverable status and leaves the cached
detection list in place. Tests cover both announcements and retained UI state.

## Approaches tried

I first used the known capture fixtures to render seeded schedule and due
reminder content. Then I loaded the actual schedule API data in the same
headless browser to confirm a server-backed list state. Direct schedule and
reminder saves returned 405. For browser workflow verification, I installed
Playwright route handlers for config, schedules, and reminders. The handlers
retained successful mutation results in process memory so a full page reload
could fetch them again. This let me verify editing and creation through the
Vue panels at desktop and mobile widths while the page itself continued to be
served by `just serve-noauth`. The test labels this simulated persistence; the
server's write boundary was neither changed nor bypassed.

For detected agents, I inspected the current PATH snapshot but did not invoke
the update-check action: the UI says that action contacts a supported public
source only when requested. The regression test uses a mocked failing response
instead, and verifies the status announcement while retaining the cached
agent row. The schedule regression test rejects the create call and verifies
the alert announcement plus the still-open editor.

## Challenges and blockers

The required `just serve-noauth` command uses the preview-child execution
boundary. Its router rejects non-GET requests before schedule, reminder, or
agent-config mutation handlers run. The Playwright stub verifies front-end
save/reload behavior but cannot prove persistence in RepoOS's file-backed
store. That limitation is recorded separately from the successful simulated
browser checks.

The initial browser probe navigated between routes in one page, which cancelled
the detected-agent SSE request during navigation. I treated those cancellation
messages as navigation artifacts and repeated checks without using them as
tab-load failures. No console finding was used to infer a product defect
without a reproducible UI symptom.

## Key learnings

The existing screen and component tests already exercise skeletons, cached
detections, refresh failures, seeded schedules, and reminder content. The QA
pass added explicit coverage where error announcements were missing. Read-only
preview behavior blocks ordinary save paths. A Playwright in-memory API store
can verify browser state across reloads, while actual durable save verification
requires a writable isolated server.
